title: Spectral synthesis with the complexity parameter
summary: We show that spectral synthesis thresholds are governed by a quantitative spectral complexity parameter, the Fourier Ratio, in addition to the geometric size of the Fourier support. In the Euclidean setting, we prove that if a compactly supported measure has finite $α$-dimensional packing measure and the associated Fourier ratio decays with asymptotic exponent $κ$, then the classical synthesis threshold improves from $\frac{2d}α$ to $\frac{2(d-2κ)}{α-2κ}$.
